patterns.comment: Type arguments. This is complicated since we don't want to match things like foo < 123 || bar > baz. A '>' in a function type arrow is content, not the end of the surrounding type arguments.

patterns.comment: Type arguments that open with '<' now and may close with '>' on a later line. Unlike #type-argument-brackets it does not require the balanced close on the same line, so it must be used only in a context that has already established these are type arguments (see the multi-line call rule). The end also bails out at a top-level statement terminator/keyword (which cannot appear in type arguments outside of a nested {...}), so a mis-fire cannot run away past the current statement.

patterns.comment: A record expression with type arguments like `MyRecord<T> {}`. The type arguments are consumed via #type-argument-brackets, then the '{' of the record body ends the rule. If no '{' follows (e.g. this was really a generic type in a value position, like the unnamed function-type parameter `(Sink<T>) => void`), the end also bails out at a statement/expression boundary so the rule cannot run away past the current statement and leak its scope downstream.
